decisions.demand: The World bench's analytics evidence (demand.json platform; twin-world ADR 0036 §8) through Rallly's own posthog-node and erasure (demand.json optional).
decisions.why: The bench exports a run's events: GET /api/projects/{id}/events/ with after, distinct_id, event, person_id, properties, limit and include_person; answers {next, results} newest first with each event's properties as sent; act 3 asserts the identified visitor's events and the guest's personless event.

sourceRules.means: events.list validates and applies filters, CSV and timestamp continuation; legacy_events_query.py owns ranges and progressive windows.
In event scope, events.distinct_id is a real column — no join needed; person_metadata chains through person.

sourceRules.means: filter.email appends an exact person property filter.
_search_match_fields tags distinct_id, email, name and id; JSON properties unrelated to these fields do not search.
A canonical UUID identifier resolves the person UUID exactly, with matched field id.
A full general page may advertise another page; previous is offset-limit only where nonnegative.
limit/offset slice the matching persons, and include_total keeps the total across pages.
tag_client_query_id refuses more than 128 characters.
An id of at most 128 characters tags the query without changing its result.
The CSV renderer sets CSV_EXPORT_LIMIT and OFFSET=0 and does not add matched_fields.

decisions.demand: posthog-js's start (posthog-js 1.290.0 packages/browser/src/remote-config.ts: RemoteConfigLoader.load loads /array/<token>/config.js, then /array/<token>/config, before it reads /flags?config=true): the World bench's browser analytics of Rallly (demand.json platform) and Cal.diy's App Store PostHog snippet (demand.json optional).
decisions.why: The World holds the project, so it holds the project's remote config, as PostHog caches it from the project's settings whenever the project is saved: RemoteConfig.build_config's fields at the settings the World's project holds, PostHog's defaults (gzip and gzip-js compression; no feature flag; performance capture on, web vitals off; the /i/v0/e/ capture endpoint; elements as a string; no suppression rule or push app; console logs, recordings, heatmaps, conversations, surveys and product tours off; identified-only persons; no site app), sanitized for the client (no siteAppsJS, no token), its keys in serde_json's default order. Answered as the hypercache server's JSON, with its cache headers. A token naming no project has no cached config: 404, empty. The token's refusals: empty 401 'Token not provided'; over 200 characters 400 'Token too long'; outside [A-Za-z0-9_-] 400 'Invalid token format'. /flags?config=true passes the same config through (evaluateFlags). posthog-js no longer falls back: it reads the script, does not read the JSON, and, the config saying hasFeatureFlags false, asks /flags only when a flag is read (remote-config.ts _onRemoteConfig). The life's act 5 asserts the script, the JSON, the unknown token and a refusal. posthog-js reaches it from the app's page, cross-origin: every answer carries the flags service's CORS (the request's Origin echoed with credentials, GET, POST, OPTIONS and HEAD, x-posthog-rate-limit-warning exposed), and a preflight is answered with it, so the browser reads the answer.

decisions.demand: posthog-js loading its lazy extensions in the app's page (posthog-js 1.290.0, Rallly's locked version, lib/src/entrypoints/external-scripts-loader.js:83: loadExternalDependency requests /static/<kind>.js?v=<version> from the assets host, requestRouter.endpointFor('assets'), surveys.js among them): the World bench's browser analytics of Rallly (demand.json platform) and Cal.diy's App Store PostHog snippet, which loads array.js from the assets host (demand.json optional).
decisions.why: PostHog serves the posthog-js bundles from its static files at /static/ (STATIC_URL), the files frontend/bin/copy-posthog-js copies from posthog-js's dist: array.js, array.full.js, array.full.es5.js, surveys.js, logs.js, exception-autocapture.js, web-vitals.js, web-vitals-with-attribution.js, tracing-headers.js, dead-clicks-autocapture.js, customizations.full.js, *integration.js, *recorder*.js, product-tours.js and conversations.js, each with its map. The pack carries those 38 files byte for byte in vendor/posthog-js/dist (with posthog-js's LICENSE) from posthog-js 1.434.14, the version PostHog's catalog pins at 80d277a5 (pnpm-workspace.yaml posthog-js: ^1.434.14, resolved by its pnpm-lock.yaml to 1.434.14): https://registry.npmjs.org/posthog-js/-/posthog-js-1.434.14.tgz, sha256 c04f4545efe749f55f4681354a6e631170f20f635183dd86e4712b208119345c. A file is served whatever its ?v query, as PostHog's static files are its one pinned build. WhiteNoise (6.10.0, PostHog's pin; its middleware answers /static/ above the CORS middleware) answers: Access-Control-Allow-Origin *, Content-Type text/javascript; charset="utf-8" for .js and application/octet-stream for .map, Cache-Control max-age=3600, public (WHITENOISE_MAX_AGE), Vary Accept-Encoding, Origin (static_varies_origin). A file outside the list is not among PostHog's static files: the ingest lane's own not-found, an empty 404 (PostHog's Django app would fall through to its signed-in frontend, which an assets host does not serve).

Access-Control-Allow-Origin * on every static file; Cache-Control max-age=<max_age>, public; a text/ type takes charset utf-8
.js is text/javascript; an unlisted extension (.map) is application/octet-stream

decisions.demand: posthog-js's startup flags request (demand.json optional: Cal.diy's App Store PostHog snippet, which loads posthog-js and calls posthog.init; Cal.diy's own posthog-js imports are never initialised at the scanned commit), and the World bench's browser analytics (demand.json platform).
decisions.why: posthog-js 1.274.1 (lib/src/posthog-featureflags.js:379-399) posts {token, distinct_id, groups, $anon_distinct_id, person_properties, group_properties} as a base64 form to /flags/?v=2&config=true and hands the answer to every extension's onRemoteConfig (sessionRecording, surveys, heatmaps, supportedCompression) before reading flags. The flags service (rust/feature-flags) checks the token (401 not_authenticated / authentication_failed, its DRF-shaped JSON) and the distinct id (400, plain text), answers FlagsV2 for v>=2 and FlagsV1 otherwise (v and config both absent mean v=2&config=true), and with config=true passes the project's remote config through at the top level (config_response_builder.rs's cache hit: the same config remoteConfig answers, built from the project the World holds). The project holds no feature flag (the private API's flag operations are unmodeled), so flags is {}. The life's act 5 asserts the v2 answer without config (the request posthog-js 1.434.11 sends when a flag is read), the v2 answer with config=true (the request Rallly's posthog-js 1.290.0 starts with), and the refusal of a key naming no project; the v1 answer and the missing-token refusal are not walked. posthog-js reaches it from the app's page, cross-origin: every answer carries the flags service's CORS (the request's Origin echoed with credentials, GET, POST, OPTIONS and HEAD, x-posthog-rate-limit-warning exposed), and a preflight is answered with it, so the browser reads the answer.

decisions.why: Rallly's posthog.init (packages/posthog/src/client.tsx:10 at 65fb5510) sets disable_session_recording: true, so its posthog-js sends nothing to /s/; a flags answer with config=true also says sessionRecording false, and one without config carries no sessionRecording at all. PostHog's docs do not document /s/'s wire (the capture service's router names the route only); it stays the gap.
